**Release:** v1.0.0, first GA\
**Date:** `2026-10-14`\
**License:** Apache 2.0\
**MCP specification:** 2025-11-25 (latest stable)\
**Platforms:** linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, windows/amd64\
**Brokers:** Solace event brokers, software and appliance, on LTS and rolling releases currently under Solace support

## Tools

- 47 tools: 29 read-only and 18 write. Write tools are disabled by default and require explicit opt-in via `enable_write_tools`.
- Read tools cover broker status and redundancy, replication, Message VPNs, queues, clients, client usernames and client profiles, REST Delivery Points, bridges, Kafka receivers and senders, discard diagnostics, and SEMP schema introspection.
- Write tools disconnect clients, delete queued messages, and clear client and queue statistics. They also create, update, and delete Message VPNs, queues, topic endpoints, and REST Delivery Points, and create and delete queue subscriptions.
- Multi-broker support, with each broker addressed by configured alias from a single server instance.

## Clients

- Compatible with any MCP client that supports the Streamable HTTP transport. Setup documented for Claude Code and Claude Desktop.
- Solace Agent Mesh integration, wiring the server into an Agent Mesh project as an MCP-tooled agent.

## Authentication and authorization

- OAuth 2.1 / OIDC for production, validated with Keycloak and Microsoft Entra ID. Unauthenticated and static-token modes available for development.
- End-user identity propagation to the broker, through OAuth token exchange or Entra On-Behalf-Of, so broker audit logs record the calling user rather than a shared service account.
- Claim-based tool authorization, gating individual tools by the group or role claim in the caller's token.

## Observability

- Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry tracing.
- Correlation ID on every request, returned to the caller and recorded in server logs and audit records.
- Metrics for tool invocations, SEMP requests, broker reachability, authentication and authorization failures, audit pipeline health, and panic recovery.
- Audit log covering every destructive operation.
- Importable Grafana dashboard and an operator runbook.
- Kubernetes liveness and readiness probes.

## Deployment

- Standalone binary, Docker image, or `go install`. Kubernetes manifests included.
- TLS terminated at the server or upstream at a proxy or ingress.
- Per-broker rate limiting, retry and backoff, and concurrency caps.
- Published checksums, plus a build provenance attestation on the release archives and the container image, verifiable against the release workflow.

## Upgrading

The server is a replacement upgrade. It holds no persistent state, so a new instance starts serving as soon as it is healthy. Open MCP sessions do not survive the swap, and clients reconnect.

Version numbering also changes at 1.0. Through the 0.x line a breaking change raised the middle number. From 1.0 it raises the first.

Upgrading from a pre-GA release may need configuration changes, and some behaviour has changed with it. The [changelog](https://github.com/SolaceProducts/solace-broker-mcp/blob/v1.0.0/CHANGELOG.md) lists every breaking change in the 0.x line. One is worth calling out, because it can break broker connectivity with an unchanged configuration file: broker traffic now follows the standard proxy environment variables where it previously went direct, so exempt your brokers, and your OTLP collector if telemetry is enabled, before upgrading.
